notation.closed_objects: Every object has exactly its listed required fields; optional fields are explicitly listed. Reject unknown fields, duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, floats where integers required and integers outside stated range. JSON encoded strict UTF-8; reject BOM, invalid UTF-8, unpaired surrogates and trailing bytes. No implicit defaults. IDs/names are case-sensitive. null is not omission.

field_types.Id: server:<lowercase UUIDv4> or draft:<lowercase UUIDv4>; server-created IDs have 122 random bits; draft IDs untrusted temporary IDs
field_types.Name: ASCII [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}, excluding Alloy keywords and generated namespace prefix allow_; names unique globally in this slice
field_types.Schema: nonempty ordered list of declared signature IDs, length 1..8
field_types.Child: expression node ID; each expression ID occurs in exactly one child position or one declaration body root
field_types.Hash: lowercase SHA-256 hex of exact bytes
field_types.Source: decoded exact UTF-8 string preserving newlines and Unicode; max 32768 UTF-8 bytes

limits.imports: NONE in either mode; SourcePolicy rejects imports rather than resolving ambient modules
limits.resource_policy: At most2 global isolated workers, at most1 combined solve/validate/commit-elaboration/canonicalization worker per durable principal; acquire shared permits before process creation. Validation queue=0: busy returns availability without new durable admission/reservation. Existing active owner retry is IN_PROGRESS or recovery, not another worker. Same existing BubblewrapLauncher isolation,512MiB Java heap,2GiB process virtual-address cap,12CPU seconds,10s external wall limit; kill/reap descendants and bound both output pipes. No inference of512MiB RSS limit from heap. Existing launcher filesystem/sandbox caps retained. Parser-spike8GiB address space is NOT deployment budget acceptance; actual launcher startup and budgets must pass before implementation acceptance, fail closed otherwise. Global cap does not relax principal cap. Complete serialized outcome<=1MiB including envelope, artifact encoding, maps, remapping and diagnostics; construct/bound outside final SQL transaction, not by individual component estimates. HTTP response may be a bounded header-only availability error on oversized result, never commit silently then claim rollback.Retain inherited500-node benchmark within512-node balanced-forest cap: measure p95 browser<50ms and server<300ms over1000 edit events on the declared reference host. No performance acceptance is inferred from budgets; empirical evidence required before any justified revision of target.

identity.principal: Server-private workspace metadata binds immutable principalId, workspaceId and logicalLaunchId to fresh bearer authority; browser cannot select these. Atomic exclusive creation, trusted canonical root, no symlink traversal, owner check, directory0700/file0600, durable flush and fail-closed corrupt/missing recovery. Resume reopens same logical scope; explicitly new launch creates distinct logical scope. Token changes never derive or replace stable IDs.
identity.node_remapping: On a new syntactically admitted request, remap each distinct draft ID injectively to a fresh server UUID before whole-module validation. References to that ID are rewritten consistently. Existing server IDs must belong to this owned document history and retain identity kind; malformed/foreign IDs reject. No client checked flag/type claim accepted. Original request bytes bind receipt; successful stored outcome contains the original-to-server ID map, so retries never rerandomize.
identity.forest: No shared expression children or bodies. Every expression has exactly one incoming ownership edge from a child slot or declaration body. Every expression reachable; no cycles; declaration references are leaves and are not ownership edges. Predicate dependency cycles reject. A moved subtree is rechecked in destination lexical environment; copy requires fresh expression/binder IDs and capture-avoiding reference remapping.

rules: IDs unique across declarations, binders, commands and expressions; declaration reference IDs resolve exact kinds. Arrays define presentation order; reference resolution never uses display text.
All derived types resolve only declared signature IDs. No inheritance, integers, relation constants, holes or imports. Expressions cannot contain declarations.
Parameters and quantifier binders may not duplicate any binder ID; lexical references must resolve within the containing predicate/body ancestry.

Field.typing: Full schema is [ownerSignatureId] ++ rangeColumns, length<=8. Unary range permits set/one/lone/some; range length>1 permits only set, printed set (B -> C ...). Reject tuple one/lone/some, no invented arrow multiplicity semantics. Owner is separate and never duplicated implicitly.

Parameter.typing: Parameter is SET-valued with this exact nominal relation schema; print explicit set multiplicity. Call arguments need exact schema, not singleton cardinality.

Command.typing: run targets only a nullary predicate; check targets only assertion. No per-signature/exact scopes or inline command formulas. Printer emits explicit options.

variable_ref.typing: exact declared binder schema in current lexical scope

predicate_call.typing: formula iff argument count and ordered exact relation schemas match parameters; no recursive dependency

union.typing: identical nonempty relation schemas -> same relation schema

intersection.typing: identical nonempty relation schemas -> same relation schema

difference.typing: identical nonempty relation schemas -> same relation schema

join.typing: left=L++[S], right=[S]++R, exact nominal endpoint S; output L++R nonempty and length<=8

all_quant.typing: formula; binder is one atom, relation [signatureId], in body only; domain is full declared signature; no disjoint/multiple binder shorthand

some_quant.typing: formula; binder is one atom, relation [signatureId], in body only; domain is full declared signature; no disjoint/multiple binder shorthand

projection.accepted_block: BLOCK_SUPPORTED contains final server-ID module, exact source, source hash, immutable artifact/source-bound occurrence/trivia maps and policy version. For SOURCE input elaborate the complete supported fragment from user declarations and predicate bodies before solver command expansion; preserve exact authored bytes. Unsupported parser-accepted policy-supported syntax is TEXT_ONLY with no invented IR. Failure or ambiguity in an otherwise claimed supported correspondence rejects or reports projection unavailable; never fabricate a graph.
projection.occurrences: Each closed occurrence has occurrenceId=nodeId+":"+role, nodeId, role, startUtf16, endUtf16. Roles are expression/operator/reference/binder; at most one interval per node/role; no path/text-based identity. Forest node ownership ensures distinct source nodes even for identical expressions. Maps bind immutable artifactId/sourceHash/exact source bytes only; immutable revision envelope supplies documentId/revision; presentationEpoch is a separate display envelope, never persisted in artifact maps. Zero-based half-open scalar-aligned UTF16 offsets; render via exact StringBuilder units. Pinned Alloy Pos line/column inclusive-end conversion must use tested UTF16 coordinate semantics, not presume byte offsets; tabs, EOF, file-reader CRLF, supplementary characters need fixtures. Reject ambiguous positions or mark location unavailable; never guess.
projection.trivia: Authoritative old trivia comes only from exact expectedRevision artifact. Retained/moved unchanged node IDs retain anchors; deleted node comments become visible trailing orphans in original order. presentationCopies explicitly duplicates source-node attached comment payloads to compatible roles on remapped fresh target nodes, ordered by original comment order then presentationCopies array index. Original trivia remains with surviving source; deletion still orphans original separately. Copy map transfers comments only, never proves an AST clone. Fresh nodes with no transfer map receive no inherited comments. No text/structural-equality inference. For SOURCE candidates preserve exact bytes and lex authoritative comment tokens: complete v1 elaboration assigns new IR IDs and node/role anchors; unsupported TEXT_ONLY stores exact comment tokens/source identity without IR or source-to-block map. Replacement BLOCK_SUPPORTED candidate from TEXT_ONLY moves all previous comments to visible trailing orphan bucket; no fabricated ownership. Existing BLOCK_SUPPORTED trivia uses deterministic smallest-enclosing expression, deepest-expression then role precedence reference,binder,operator,expression, with leading/trailing boundary ties fixed; ambiguity goes to visible orphan bucket. Comment slices stored once with original byte order and anchor (copy intentionally duplicates payload). Unchanged source exact; changed whitespace may regenerate. Source replacement is explicit authority for its authored comments; block edits preserve/transfer old payloads as above and must parse/remap successfully.
projection.draft_freshness: draftId, draftEpoch and exactSourceHash bind diagnostics. Increment epoch on every edit/document/selection/bounds/undo transition. Current evidence additionally requires full accepted analysis key and draft equals accepted source.
projection.structural_equivalence: Ordered typed trees equal modulo explicit declaration/signature/binder-ID bijection, transparent parser NOOP wrappers and ordered associative AND/OR flattening only. Preserve other operator tags, column order, multiplicity, predicate-call target, all/some distinction and command options. Expanded Command.formula is not an authored-tree oracle.

api.common: Versioned /api/v1/documents endpoints. Request objects closed; path documentId supplied once, not duplicated in body. Server derives all principal/workspace/launch scope. Responses have protocol=1, requestId, status, data; status-specific data objects closed. No browser authority/type/validation Boolean fields.

create.response: new documentId, revision=0, empty accepted module/source/maps and policyVersion; creation receipt scoped to workspace and reserved creation namespace. Workspace lock serializes key/create quota. Revision zero is valid empty BLOCK_SUPPORTED module, no command.

read.response: authorized immutable revision/artifact/provenance, or current head. Never return another scope existence. Indefinite history is readable subject to output bounds.

validateDraft.response: draftId,draftEpoch,exactSourceHash,baseRevision,supportMode,diagnostics; advisory only, no checked-candidate token or accepted revision

commit.response: COMMITTED: revision,artifact,sourceHash,policyVersion,idRemapping,provenance; terminal rejected outcome: code,acceptedRevision,diagnostics. Receipt contains exact response.

Candidate.variant_rule: Exactly one of two closed variants; no edit-program language in v1. Browser applies edits to full immutable candidate then submits whole candidate.

presentationCopies.sourceNodeId: existing server ID in exact expectedRevision artifact
presentationCopies.targetNodeId: fresh draft ID present in submitted candidate

Candidate.presentationCopies_rules: Required closed array, empty if none, at most512 entries; each entry has exactly sourceNodeId and targetNodeId. Exact original request bytes bind mapping. Source must exist in authorized exact base artifact; target must be a newly created draft ID in this complete candidate, remapped by server, and each destination appears once. One source may have multiple destinations. Source/target node kind and transferable closed roles must match. This authorizes only comment transfer, never certifies subtree cloning or structural equality: user may edit copied content before commit. No client trivia payload, source spans or checked flag accepted. Validate map before transferring comments; invalid mapping is deterministic INVALID_DRAFT.

undoRedo.response: Same commit envelope; revalidation creates a fresh checked artifact under current policy and a fresh revision with targetRevision/direction provenance. Exact source unchanged may reuse immutable map CONTENT bytes, but artifact identity/envelope is fresh; no prior maps or artifacts mutate. Map contents contain no old revision authority.

analyze.response: jobId/full accepted analysis key; command owns explicit bounded options from accepted revision. Historical evidence separately labeled.

errors.rules: After strict envelope admission and quota reservation, deterministic whole-module validation errors and stale outcomes receive immutable receipts. Authentication/malformed/availability/pre-admission capacity failure never does. Runtime resource timeout is availability, not deterministic validation. Receipt conflict never overwrites original receipt. HTTP transport failure cannot establish rollback.

receipts.request_identity: Store exact original HTTP body bytes (no JSON canonicalization) plus SHA256 and method/route/API version; transport whitespace/key order differences are changed bytes. Client persists exact body for retry. Key is also inside body; scoped unique key is principal/logicalLaunch/workspace/document/key. Digest collision never substitutes for exact equality.
receipts.retention: All receipts and history retained indefinitely in this bounded local slice; no expiry or deletion API or cleanup job. Thus 24h and active retry windows are retained without clock-based lifecycle. Backup/restore retains all scoped identities and receipts.
receipts.lookup: Authenticate/authorize document then bounded envelope parse then receipt lookup before quota rejection, remapping, parser or stale check. Identical stored body returns original stored response; changed bytes rejects. Repeat lookup under final lock, including for deterministic validation errors.
receipts.quota: Per workspace hard limits: 64 documents, 4096 revisions, 16384 receipts, 256 MiB accounted artifact/request/response bytes. Track durable usage and admission reservations under workspace lock. Reserve worst-case 4 MiB per admitted mutating request and one receipt slot plus possible revision slot; reject new admission if exhausted. Existing receipt lookups remain readable at quota. Reclaim only unused reservation after known outcome; abandoned reservations require recovery of commit certainty, never history deletion. Reservation payload ceiling covers original request<=256KiB, stored artifact<=1MiB, stored terminal response<=1MiB and admission/request duplication<=256KiB; accounting metadata charged conservatively within 4MiB. SQL/WAL/index/physical disk overhead excluded and monitored independently; physical capacity failure is availability, never false rollback certainty. Document limit includes document_count + reserved_documents. Each admitted CREATE reserves one document slot and revision0 slot under workspace lock; with63 documents only one pending CREATE can be admitted. Preserve reservations across takeover. Successful token-fenced creation converts its document/revision reservation to used counters; deterministic failure or verified recoverable abandonment releases unused reservations atomically. No release on unknown commit outcome until receipt/transaction certainty recovered. Before admission enforce request/component ceilings; before final transaction construct and bound full terminal response and artifact bytes.4MiB reservation is a conservative bound, not permission to emit an oversized component. Known serialization/output failure is availability, retains recoverable admission and writes no terminal receipt.
receipts.outcome: Store immutable response envelope/status and ID remapping. Replay returns original outcome even after later revisions/policy upgrades; response labels receipt replay and separately supplies current revision if requested, never changes original outcome. Successful receipt and accepted revision atomic; rejected receipt and unchanged document atomic.

storage.namespace: Dedicated documents schema owned by NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS owner; allow_app is neither table owner nor BYPASSRLS. No raw SQL public interface. All SQL including migration/restore/transaction control through SQLean proxy using existing sql_connections.connect; no new JDBC path.
storage.scope_settings: Fixed literal SELECT set_config('allow.tenant',%s,true) with durable principalId; allow.project with workspaceId; allow.purpose='document'. These existing admitted keys need no new guard GUC names. Do not instantiate retrieval.Repository with purpose=document (its purpose allowlist intentionally differs). Separate narrow store bridge reuses connection plumbing only.
storage.columns: Every table includes principal_id, workspace_id; scoped identities below include both. Logical launch partitions receipts but does not partition durable document ownership/history.

workspace.rules: Server provisioned; counters nonnegative; limits immutable versioned policy. Policy update locks this row.

logical_launch.rules: Private metadata-bound immutable launch registration; never browser provisioned.

document.rules: Head references same scoped revision with deferred FK; revision 0 inserted atomically with document. Only head/title mutable.

artifact.rules: Immutable; TEXT_ONLY module/map null; BLOCK_SUPPORTED all required. Hash never sole byte equality authority.

revision.rules: Immutable; revision monotone head+1. Direction/target both present for history-copy only; artifact references always same document.

receipt.rules: Immutable; document_namespace is documentId or reserved CREATE namespace; successful result FK includes scope and document/revision. Noncreate receipt document FK same scope; create outcomes bind created document. No expiry column or cleanup.

admission.rules: Serializes same-key active work and durable quota reservation; state ADMITTED/VALIDATING/FINALIZING/TERMINAL. Each ownership generation has server incarnation and fresh CSPRNG owner_nonce. No lease expiry takeover. Takeover requires verified old owned process reaping or verified prior incarnation exit and new owner_nonce installed under workspace/document locks. Every finalization compares exact current owner_nonce and request bytes; old checked frames are fenced out even if old validation returns. Preserve reservation through takeover; recover committed receipt first. No cleanup of history/receipt and no inference of rollback from child timeout. Bind method/route/API version in active row and checked frame as well as original body. CREATE reserves document=1 and revision=1 (revision0 counts); all other operations document=0. State/counter settlement requires current owner_nonce under ordered locks. Terminal admissions retained and all retained request/outcome/metadata copies charged exactly once; unused reservations release atomically.

storage.rls: ENABLE and FORCE RLS on every table; USING and WITH CHECK compare principal_id=current_setting(allow.tenant,true) and workspace_id=current_setting(allow.project,true) and purpose=document. Missing settings deny. Scoped composite FKs prevent cross-document/workspace references. Revoke PUBLIC schema/table privileges, no app CREATE/TRUNCATE. Grant SELECT/INSERT on immutable tables, UPDATE only on document head/title and quota/admission control columns; no app UPDATE/DELETE on history/artifact/receipt. No SECURITY DEFINER bypass in v1.
storage.lock_order: READ COMMITTED transactions; trusted scope settings transaction-local. Always workspace row FOR UPDATE first, then document row FOR UPDATE when applicable, then scoped admission/receipt key. No reverse acquisition. Workspace lock serializes quota, policy, same-key reservation and final CAS locally; no advisory-key hash collision dependence. Initial receipt read is advisory; all mutation decisions repeat under this order. Never hold transaction while parsing/worker subprocess runs.
protocol: Authenticate/bind scope; strict bounded envelope parse; authorized existing receipt lookup before parser/quota.

Short admission transaction locks workspace/document, repeats receipt lookup, compares active key exact bytes, reserves quota and creates durable admission. Concurrent identical in-flight request returns IN_PROGRESS availability response or waits outside SQL transaction then repeats lookup; changed bytes denies. CREATE additionally checks document_count+reserved_documents<64 and atomically reserves one document slot and revision0. Receipt-only failed outcomes release revision/document reservation and account retained failure data; no quota oversubscription between distinct pending CREATE keys.

Outside SQL transaction only the admitted owner_nonce holder validates: freeze original bytes, remap IDs, whole-module/parser/maps validation; immutable checked frame binds owner_nonce, scope/document/base, original bytes, final artifact bytes and current policy/dependency versions. Never browser supplied. Reap bounded worker before ownership recovery. Availability leaves no terminal receipt and retains recoverable admission reservation.

Final short transaction locks workspace/document, then scoped admission key; repeat authorized receipt lookup FIRST. Existing identical outcome returns unchanged regardless of current stale/validation result; conflicting bytes deny. Otherwise compare admission exact bytes and current owner_nonce, authorization and policy fence. New success additionally requires checked-artifact binding and head=expectedRevision; atomically insert artifact/revision, advance head, insert immutable success receipt and settle reservation/counters. Deterministic validation/stale rejection atomically inserts immutable terminal receipt, settles reservation, leaves head untouched. Validation failures still require current nonce and policy fence; changed policy requests outside-transaction revalidation rather than recording obsolete validation outcome. Database errors known rolled back create no receipt; uncertain acknowledgement returns UNKNOWN_COMMIT_OUTCOME. Final nonce checks bind method/route/API version. Workspace/document counter settlement includes reserved_documents and revision0. If nonce stale, no mutation or terminal receipt; old owner cannot release current owner reservation.

Known rollback reports no commit. Connection/ack loss after commit sent yields UNKNOWN_COMMIT_OUTCOME; retain same request/key and query/retry. Never assert previous revision unchanged on an uncertain acknowledgement. A new bridge invocation must recover committed receipt before any new attempt.
